name: Sports Hernia / Inguinal-Related Groin Pain
definition: Groin pain clinically localized to the inguinal canal region, often provoked by abdominal resistance or Valsalva, without necessarily having a palpable true hernia.

typical: Pain with cough/strain or resisted sit-up
No obvious hernia may be present

investigations.principle: Ultrasound/MRI are selective; diagnosis remains clinical after exclusion of true hernia and other causes.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, cartilage, tendon, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent symptoms may warrant general-surgery/sports evaluation.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vankshana-shoola phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Groin pain clinically localized to the inguinal canal region, often provoked by abdominal resistance or Valsalva, without necessarily having a palpable true hernia.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, severe deformity, progressive weakness, suspected tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
